If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, shift forecast midpoint downward by 1.0–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is mixed (±0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.3–0.7% to forecast for late horizon (16–30 days) to account for momentum carryover.

If sentiment is mixed and price is trending downward, subtract 0.3–0.7% from forecast for late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is uniformly positive but price is flat or slightly declining, reduce forecast by 0.2–0.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to prevent overconfidence in bullish signal.
